terms.gloss: the last syllable of a word, the ultima
evidence: Quint. 12.10.33: quia ultima syllaba nec acūta unquam excitātur nec flexa circumdūcitur
terms.comment: ultima alone also serves; Latin almost never stresses it: Quandō accentus pōnitur in ultimā syllabā? — Numquam aut utique rārissimē. (Traupman 238).

phrases.latin: sed accentūs quoque … minus suāvēs habēmus, quia ultima syllaba nec acūta unquam excitātur nec flexa circumdūcitur
phrases.english: our accents too are less pleasing, because the last syllable is never raised by an acute nor drawn round by a circumflex

sources: Lewis & Short: ultimus · Lewis & Short: syllaba
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 238, p. 247.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
